item.title: Judge dismisses charges against billionaire Adani, but sharply criticizes DOJ
item.description: A federal judge dismissed fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani at the DOJ's request. But in an unusual twist, he refused to dismiss charges against some co-defendants and criticized the DOJ's handling of the case.

item.title: Trump signs order on vaccination recommendations
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on childhood vaccine schedules Monday.

item.title: Mother, 5-month-old die in New York Harbor after boat capsized; captain charged
item.description: Manuel Hernandez, the boat's 46-year-old captain, was arrested on reckless endangerment charges and also charged in federal court with two counts of misconduct and neglect.

item.title: How Trump achieved his 2024 political comeback
item.description: A recently released book examines how President Trump secured his party's 2024 nomination despite his 2020 election loss and numerous criminal indictments. Seth Masket, author of "The Elephants in the Room," joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Sen. Chuck Grassley bids farewell to 49-year-old vacuum cleaner
item.description: Republican Sen. Chuck Grassley of Iowa has said goodbye to a beloved member of his family: a nearly 50-year-old vacuum cleaner named Beth. Political strategists Marc Short and Carolyn Bourdeaux join to discuss.

item.title: 7.4 earthquake strikes western Colombia, killing over 100 people
item.description: The 7.4 magnitude earthquake's epicenter was San José del Palmar, about 250 miles west of Colombia's capital, Bogota, officials said.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's psychiatrist completes testimony with tense exchange
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's first psychiatrist was back on the witness stand Monday, completing her testimony in the Massachusetts murder trial.

item.title: Enes Freedom declares for WNBA draft in protest of trans athletes
item.description: Former NBA player-turned-conservative-activist Enes Freedom has submitted a letter of intent declaring for the WNBA draft in a protest against trans athletes in women's sports. AP basketball writer Doug Feinberg and former gymnast Jennifer Sey join to discuss.

item.title: Powerball jackpot reaches $905M for tonight's drawing as prize surges
item.description: With no winner since May, the Powerball grand prize ballooned to the eighth largest in history​.

item.title: California House candidate Connie Chan says opponent created a chatbot that mocked her accent
item.description: California congressional candidate Scott Wiener has deleted an AI chatbot his campaign made that mimics his opponent, Connie Chan. Wiener says it was meant to highlight Chan's record on issues like public housing, but critics say it mocked her with racist and sexist connotations. Chan joins "The Takeout" with her reaction.

item.title: Previewing primaries in South Carolina, Minnesota
item.description: Several states are holding primaries on Tuesday. This includes governor and senator contests in Minnesota and the primary to replace the late Sen. Lindsey Graham in South Carolina. CBS News' Mark Strassmann and Jonah Kaplan report.

item.title: Examining Trump's options for ending Iran stalemate
item.description: President Trump told Axios that he is only "semi-negotiating" with Tehran. The Iranians are demanding that they be compensated for war damage to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. CBS News national security contributor Samantha Vinograd joins with analysis.

item.title: Unpacking possible impacts from Trump's order on childhood vaccines
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on Monday that could dramatically overhaul the way parents and children receive and regard scientifically-proven vaccines for a wide array of diseases. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe and Dr. Jon LaPook join with the latest.

item.title: WNBA player DiJonai Carrington ejected after foul against Sophie Cunningham, sparking controversy
item.description: Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington was ejected and hit with a Flagrant 2 foul for a block against Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham. The moment escalated when both players had to be held back from each other. When referees were asked why Cunningham was not issued a technical foul for pushing Carrington after the play, the refs said the reaction was acceptable given the severity of the initial contact. Yahoo Sports women's basketball reporter Cassandra Negley has more.

item.title: Doctor urges parents to "ignore what the president is saying" about vaccines
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on Monday that outlined new recommendations for childhood vaccinations. The order, obtained by CBS News before signing, said it would reduce the number of recommended vaccines and encouraged parents to spread children's shots across separate visits to the doctor. Dr. Richard Besser, a pediatrician and CEO of the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Meta launches new AI model as Sen. Bernie Sanders calls for more regulation
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders on Monday called for more regulation of artificial intelligence, saying companies are losing control of the technology. On the same day, Meta released a new AI tool. Axios tech and policy reporter Maria Curi joins to discuss.

item.title: More than 100 killed in Colombian earthquake
item.description: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck Colombia about 250 miles west of Bogotá on Monday. CBS News immigration correspondent Camilo Montoya-Galvez has the latest.

item.title: Court clears way for social media addiction suits against tech giants
item.description: Appeals court ruling could open the door to a flood of litigation against Google, Meta and other social media players.

item.title: Trump demands Iran pay compensation following new conditions for reopening strait
item.description: President Trump signaled he would be piling economic pressure on Iran as the stalemate continued and Tehran laid out new conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Why Taylor Farms faces scrutiny over salmonella and cyclospora outbreaks
item.description: Despite a rash of foodborne illnesses in recent months, one expert said the nation's food supply is "remarkably safe." Here's what to know.

item.title: Contiguous U.S. breaks its record for hottest month ever, NOAA says
item.description: Temperatures last month averaged 76.9 degrees Fahrenheit as above-average warmth blanketed the U.S.

item.title: Watch: Trump signs executive order updating childhood vaccine recommendations
item.description: President Trump on Monday signed an executive order laying out new recommendations for childhood vaccines. Lindsey Reiser anchored CBS News' live coverage.

item.title: Why are gold prices falling? 4 factors that are impacting gold's value
item.description: Gold prices have dropped quite a bit this year. Here's what's behind the drop (and why it may be a good time to buy in).

item.title: Big Bear bald eagle Jackie has died, California veterinary center says
item.description: "It is with profound sadness that we share that [Jackie] passed away in the early hours of this morning, following more than three weeks of intensive medical care," Ojai Raptor Center said.

item.title: What to know after Netanyahu rejects Trump's Gaza peace plan
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected a U.S.-backed peace plan for Gaza that would've called for the Israeli military to gradually withdraw from parts of Gaza as Hamas disarmed. CBS News contributor Robert Berger reports.

item.title: How much interest can a $75,000 high-yield savings account earn over the next year?
item.description: Have $75,000 to transfer into a high-yield savings account? Here's how much interest you'd earn over the next year.

item.title: Meta launches new AI model for home as Mark Zuckerberg pushes for open-source strategy
item.description: Meta is launching a version of its most powerful AI model that allows people to code from home. Ina Fried, chief technology correspondent for Axios, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Blanche sworn in as attorney general, formally taking reins at DOJ
item.description: Todd Blanche was sworn in as attorney general after the Senate narrowly voted to confirm the president's former defense lawyer to helm the Justice Department over the weekend.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg's yacht missed boat's call for help, spokesperson says
item.description: The issue arose when a skiff ran out of fuel off the coast of Alaska and called for assistance from nearby ships.

item.title: 1 dead, 3 missing after boat sinks near Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay
item.description: One person died and three were missing in San Francisco Bay on Tuesday after a boat with 20 people on board sank near Alcatraz Island, authorities said.
